panels.is: Shot 3, Tony Blair seated, grinning at an unseen interviewer off-frame left, in an oak-panelled library; behind him a chase: dinner guests and a butler fleeing across the room, a wolf at their heels. He ignores it (that is the joke).
The same shot later: two guests have just run past, two wolves follow them.

Frames with their times (read left to right, top to bottom): the double doors at the back fly open; a butler carrying a tray of champagne flutes bursts out toward us, swerves left and the tray flies on, tumbling; three guests follow, each with a wolf at their heels, splitting left and right round the room.
Frames with their times: two of them come back across together, left to right, one nearer us leading, then their two wolves behind.
Frames with their times: the other two come back right to left the same way, then their wolves.

Frames with their times: a third pair right to left with their wolves; the room empties; the butler runs in again from the left; at 26.75 a huge wolf leaps in at the top right toward Blair's head (the film cuts before it reaches him).
Frames 1/12 s apart, the left half of the room: the flying tray hops once and rattles flat on the floor; the flutes land and shatter, each leaving a pool of champagne that stays.
Frames 1/24 s apart, close: the butler mid-run, side on (partly hidden by Blair at the right).
